opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $398M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up from $6M a year ago as the sales effort scaled.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration; up from $48M a year ago.

follow100Note: The striking thing: interest and other non-operating costs took $24.05 of every $100 — and running the platform took another $60.43. A $15M tax benefit added back $0.95, but the business still lost $28.75 of every $100 it took in.
footerNote: Gross profit = revenue less cost of revenue. The $452M net loss is drawn as 'Covered by cash on hand'.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted net loss per share, vs -$0.34 a year ago

kpis.label: Capex
kpis.note: purchases of property and equipment in Q4 alone

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation of $157M is stripped out of the adjusted figures: the non-GAAP reconciliation removes $157M of stock-based compensation, $11M of amortization of acquired intangibles, $9M of acquisition-related costs and a $4M loss on extinguishment of debt on the way from the GAAP net loss of $452M to the adjusted net loss of $284M. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter. Adjusted operating income (non-GAAP) was $88M and adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $898M, a 57% margin.
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $378M: interest expense, net was $388M — the cost of borrowing heavily to build data centers — partly offset by $10M of other income, net. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter. The tax line was a $15M benefit, not a bill.

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out GPU-powered cloud capacity purpose-built for AI training and inference (running trained models); the company's single revenue line, up 110% YoY as demand from AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises surged.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $1,572M, up from $747M a year ago, and the revenue backlog — work customers have committed to — reached $66.8B at quarter-end, more than four times where the year began.
takeaways.title: Revenue more than doubled

takeaways.text: Operations lost $89M, but net interest expense was $388M. After $10M of other income and a $15M tax benefit, the net loss was $452M — the price of borrowing to build ahead of demand.
takeaways.title: Interest is what makes the loss bigger

takeaways.text: CoreWeave spent $4,060M on property and equipment in the quarter — about 2.6 times its revenue — while operating cash flow was $1,559M. Active power passed 850 MW after adding about 260 MW in the quarter, with about 3.1 GW contracted.
takeaways.title: Spending to build is enormous

verdict: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $1.6B and its backlog reached $66.8B, but $388M of net interest turned an $89M operating loss into a $452M net loss.
